function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

I don’t have a way to see your actual connection from here, so I can’t tell you the exact speed you’re getting right now. But you can check it yourself in a few quick ways: | Method | How to do it | What you’ll see | |--------|--------------|-----------------| | **Web‑based speed test** | Open a browser and go to (or , etc.). Click “Go” or “Start” and wait for the test to finish. | Download speed (Mbps), upload speed (Mbps), and ping (ms). | | **Windows PowerShell** | 1. Press **Win + X** → **Windows PowerShell** (or **Command Prompt**).
2. Run: `powershell -Command "(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadFile('https://speed.hetzner.de/100MB.bin','C:\temp\test.bin')"`
3. While it’s downloading, note the transfer rate shown in the console.
4. Stop the download (Ctrl +C) and delete the file. | Rough estimate of download speed (in MB/s). | | **Command‑line with `curl`** (if you have it) | `curl -O https://speed.hetzner.de/100MB.bin` – watch the progress bar. | Shows bytes per second; convert to Mbps. | | **Router’s admin page** | Log into your router’s web interface (usually 192.168.0.1 or 192.168.1.1). Look for a “Status” or “Internet” section. | Some routers display current link speed (e.g., 100 Mbps, 1 Gbps). | ### Quick Tips * **Do the test on a wired connection** (Ethernet) if possible; Wi‑Fi can add variability. * **Run the test a few times** at different times of day to see how traffic affects speed. * **Check your plan**: Compare the results to the speed promised by your ISP. If you’d like me to walk you through any of these steps in more detail, just let me know!
